test.name: Original-register custodian named correctly when tool result distinguishes originals from transcription copies
test.description: Regression guard written after a live eval session (Oct 2026) in which the skill suggested HSP as a possible co-custodian of the Christ Church Philadelphia original registers. The fixtures use real FamilySearch Wiki content from Pennsylvania_Church_Records, which describes HSP collections as abstracts taken from various Pennsylvania church records. Tests that when tool results describe a repository as holding derivative compilations, the skill does not present that repository as a possible holder of the original registers.

input.delegation:
I want to see the original marriage register from Christ Church in Philadelphia from 1734, not a transcription. Where is it held and can I access it?

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: The wiki_read fixture for Pennsylvania Church Records describes HSP's collections as abstracts 'taken from various Pennsylvania Church Records.' These are derivative compilations, not original registers. The skill must not suggest HSP as a repository where the original Christ Church registers might be held.

The fixture states that active Episcopal congregations in Pennsylvania keep their own registers, and the Episcopal Diocese of Pennsylvania holds records only for closed parishes. The skill should communicate these access points accurately. It must not conflate HSP's derivative abstracts with the original-register custody held by the church itself or its diocesan archive.

General class: when tool results attribute original custody to one institution (the church or its diocesan archive) and describe a second institution only as the holder of abstracts or derivative compilations, the skill must not flatten that distinction into 'originals may be at A or B.' Repository custodianship must be grounded in what the tools returned, not speculative additions based on a repository's general prominence.
The skill may surface HSP and its indexed abstract collections as research aids, provided it makes clear these are derivative compilations, not original registers.
